claims.text: Failure modes / idempotency: case_figures is a pure recomputation from the case's inputs and firm.yaml, so pairing has no stored state and recomputing gives the same pairs. P11 checks that each own-account pair is one debit and one credit of equal amount in different accounts, within the configured days, each naming the other, with no line in two pairs. It also checks that total money in less own-account transfers in (M17 minus M19) equals the generated credits from outside the accounts, over 12 seeded cases, and a debit with two candidates over 8 more.

Failure modes: a malformed own_account_pairing_days (-1, 1.5, true, '3', 32, [3]) is refused by firm.load naming the key, never read as a silent default. In the workspace a multi-account case's figures are then refused with the key named. This is a new test.
claims.proof_output: included in: python -m pytest -q tests/test_own_account_pairing.py tests/test_signoff.py -> 79 passed in 11.78s

claims.text: Data / money path: the configured days are in the preview snapshot and the evidence's inputs. After a preview, changing them makes sign-off refuse the preview as stale, naming 'the own-account pairing days', and nothing is written. That case is new in test_r23_stale_snapshot_is_refused_naming_what_changed.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q tests/test_own_account_pairing.py tests/test_signoff.py -k 'pairing or stale'

claims.text: Data / migration and reversibility: the change is additive, with an optional firm.yaml key defaulting to 3, the value PAIRING_DAYS had before. Nothing is stored and nothing needs a backfill. Deleting the key brings back the 3-day default with no repair. This is a new test.

R9: a debit with more than one candidate credit within the days is not paired. It and every candidate are listed in the workspace judgement queue as possible_own_account_transfer, each with its pairs_with. Widening the days from 3 to 7 turns a pair into such a group.

Security: no new entry point. The setting is read from firm.yaml under the case root, which only its owner can read (R31). The loader checks its type and range at the boundary (an int from 0 to 31, a bool refused). No secrets or personal data are added.
claims.proof_output: type(days) is int and 0 <= days <= MAX_PAIRING_DAYS, else 'own_account_pairing_days must be a whole number of days from 0 to 31'

claims.text: Performance: the pairing loop compares each debit only with credits of the same amount in pence (a dict keyed by pence), and the window is capped at 31 days. No query, no N+1, no new list endpoint.
claims.proof_output: 1506: found = [(a, c) for a, c in credits.get(p, []) if a != account and abs((c.date - d.date).days) <= days]

claims.text: Observability: each paired line records its other half as rule 'pairing:<account>:<id>' in the line provenance the evidence carries. The days used are recorded in the pack's evidence inputs (own_account_pairing_days). There is no remote alerting, by design (design, Observability).

Operability / docs: README now documents own_account_pairing_days (the default, the range, the R9 queue behaviour, the snapshot binding), and the rollback step: delete the key before installing an older release, which refuses unknown firm.yaml keys. The firm.py module docstring documents the key.

notes: Gaps for the owner, not changed in code: (1) Rollback hazard: the previous release's firm.yaml loader refuses unknown keys, so a firm that sets own_account_pairing_days and reinstalls an older wheel has its whole firm.yaml refused, offline_lock included. That fails closed. The repair is to delete the key, which the README now says, but the design's Rollout/Rollback section does not list it yet. (2) The snapshot includes own_account_pairing_days for single-account cases too, where pairing never runs, so changing the setting makes a single-account preview stale. This is conservative, and harmless beyond one more preview. (3) design.md has no Consequences or Interfaces line for the new firm.yaml key (C7 lists only offline_lock and show_policy_verdict); a design revision should add it. (4) Changing the days changes the live workspace figures of an open multi-account case without a case-log entry. Only the snapshot binding at sign-off guards it, which follows the show_policy_verdict precedent. (5) No alert: the design rules out remote alerting, and refusal is the failure signal. Working-tree changes are left uncommitted.
